prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a sloped ground plane in an outdoor brickyard where the camera wearer walks forward from left to right across the 5 frames toward a crouching person in a blue shirt. In frame 1, a tall stack of bricks on the right edge (0.8 to 2.5 m away) and a closer clay mound on the lower left (1.5 m away) appear bright, while the crouching worker is roughly 3.5 to 4 m ahead behind a second clay mound (2.5 to 3 m away), with flat rows of drying bricks to the worker's right and a hoe and wheelbarrow 3 to 5 m away on the left. Across frames 2 to 5, the camera wearer approaches and looks steeply downward until standing directly above the worker (about 1 to 1.2 m from the head-mounted camera in frame 5, with the camera wearer's own lower legs visible at the bottom edge within 1 m), while the first clay mound and right-side brick stack pass out of view and the second clay mound shifts from the lower foreground in frame 3 (1 m away) to the upper right in frame 5 (1.2 m away). The map makes the 3D relief of the raised clay mounds, the stepped height of the right-hand brick stack, and the elevated head and torso of the crouching worker above the flat ground plane much clearer than the similarly coloured brown surfaces in the RGB strip. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 5 where the global contrast rescales and makes the surrounding ground and clay mound appear abnormally dark and distant relative to the worker, and it blurs fine boundaries around the hoe handle and individual flat bricks.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the crouching worker (`person`) across all 5 frames as the camera wearer approaches from about 4 m away in frame 1 to roughly 1 m directly overhead in frame 5, shifting the worker's image position from the upper-left quadrant to the lower-centre foreground. In frame 1, the map also segments the vertical stack of bricks along the right edge (0.8 to 2.5 m away, with blue cloth resting on top) into two adjacent masks, while the worker sits 1.5 to 2 m to the left of the flat brick grid and just behind a clay mound that stays within the worker's arm's reach (0.3 to 0.5 m) across all frames. As the camera wearer moves closer and tilts downward across frames 3 to 5, the `person` mask captures the worker turning from facing forward/downward toward the camera wearer in frame 3 to facing rightward toward the clay mound in frame 4 and forward/upward toward the clay mound in frame 5, along with the head-mounted camera strap on the worker's head. This map clearly separates the worker's silhouette—including the outstretched right arm reaching to a brick in frame 3 and the camera wearer's own legs at the bottom of frame 5—from the similarly toned brown soil and bricks in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable because it misclassifies the right-hand brick stack in frame 1 as `bench` and `suitcase`, merges the camera wearer's lower legs at the bottom of frame 5 into the crouched worker's `person` mask, and completely fails to segment the clay mounds, flat brick rows, hoe, and wheelbarrow.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects a yellow body skeleton only in frame 3, where the crouching worker is centred about 2 m in front of and below the camera wearer, between the foreground clay mound (1 m away) and the flat rows of bricks immediately to the right. In this frame, the skeleton shows the worker in a deep squat with torso pitched forward, head tilted slightly down while facing generally toward the camera wearer, left arm bent near the knee, and right arm extended downward and to the right within arm's reach (under 0.5 m) of the brick mold on the ground and the nearby clay mound. The skeleton clarifies the compact, folded limb geometry of the worker's squat in frame 3, where the dark limbs and shadow under the torso blend together in the RGB image. However, the pose map is largely unreliable across the sequence because it completely misses the worker's body in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5—when the worker is either farther away (3 to 4 m in frames 1 and 2) or viewed from a steep overhead angle while turned toward the clay mound (1 to 1.5 m away in frames 4 and 5)—and it fails to detect any magenta hand skeletons or the camera wearer's partially visible legs in frame 5.
